runbooks.title: Code Nest availability
runbooks.objective: Determine whether the application, reverse proxy, or host is responsible for lost availability.
triageSteps: Compare the internal application target with the external HTTP probe.
Check the latest deployment snapshot and application start time.
Review bounded HTTP error, latency, JVM, CPU, and disk evidence.
Escalate for operator action when the host or reverse proxy is unavailable.
escalationSignals: Both internal and external availability signals are unavailable.
The external probe fails while the internal application target remains healthy.
A recent deployment aligns with the first failed observation.

runbooks.title: Code Nest SRE runtime
runbooks.objective: Identify queue, lease, deadline, or read-only investigation degradation without changing system state.
triageSteps: Compare backlog size with the oldest queued item age.
Review retry, lease recovery, deadline, and terminal failure counters.
Check worker start time and the immutable deployment provenance.
Use the stored run trajectory to identify the last completed bounded step.
escalationSignals: A queue contains terminal failures or deadline violations.
Lease recovery continues after a worker restart.
Read-only investigation failures exceed the configured alert threshold.

runbooks.title: Code Nest default investigation
runbooks.objective: Build a bounded timeline from persisted alerts, metrics, deployment provenance, and incident evidence.
triageSteps: Confirm the alert state, severity, service, and first observation time.
Compare the current metric snapshot with the persisted alert snapshot.
Check whether a recent deployment aligns with the incident timeline.
Record missing evidence as a limitation and request operator review.
escalationSignals: The available evidence cannot distinguish application and host failure.
The incident remains active after the bounded investigation ends.
The recommended next step requires a system change.
